rules.title: Statewide cap and conditions on tenant screening fees
rules.requirement: A landlord's screening fee can't be more than the yearly maximum, which Berkeley lists as $68.96 for 2026. You should get a receipt with itemized costs, a copy of any credit report, and a refund of any unused part of the fee. A landlord can't charge the fee if no unit is actually available. The fee must be returned to applicants who aren't selected unless the landlord reviews applications in order and doesn't charge applicants it never considers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental applicants in California when a landlord charges a screening fee.

rules.title: Required tenant screening fee rights statement and fee cap disclosure
rules.requirement: Before taking a screening or application fee in Berkeley, the owner must give you a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the maximum fee allowed under Civil Code § 1950.6(b). These must appear in the application or in a separate disclosure.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of residential property in Berkeley who charge an applicant a fee for a consumer credit report or to process an application.

rules.title: Ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenants (renewals and roommates)
rules.requirement: A Berkeley landlord can't charge a current tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees for a roommate leaving and fees to add or replace a roommate. Lease terms that say otherwise can't be enforced.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, regardless of contrary lease language (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate
rules.penalty: Lease provisions that violate the chapter are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018).

notes: The $68.96 figure for 2026 comes from the Berkeley Rent Board page. It is the CPI-adjusted state cap under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The rule that a landlord must accept a reusable screening report is mentioned without its own citation. It likely comes from Civ. Code § 1950.1, so it is folded into the § 1950.6 record and not given a separate record. BMC 13.78.018, which makes the chapter apply to existing agreements, is noted in the § 13.78.016 record. The document gives no effective dates. The page says the URL for the fee rights statement has not yet been provided by the City.
